ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Although ‘human being’ is general, context identifies the Quraysh miscreants who arrogantly evaded God’s Book and Messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Almighty referred to them by a general word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The phrase about turning aside intensifies evasion: polite evasion is possible, but hatred makes a person physically turn away too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: when a person evades something because of hate and dislike, he physically turns away too

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People should show gratitude in ease and patience in trials; instead, blessings make the opponents arrogant enough to demand punishment, and any seizure would come too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: favours have made them arrogant to such an extent that they demand a sign of punishment

BURSEVI:v5p150/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150/r1.speaker: الشيخ التميمي
BURSEVI:v5p150/r1.claim: Al-Tamimi says washing the sick person's face with water from a vessel on which Fatiha was written can cure by God's permission; drinking it may ease trembling, doubts, and palpitations, while a rosewater remedy restores poor memory.
BURSEVI:v5p150/r1.anchor: قال الشيخ التميمي رحمه الله في "خواص القرآن" : إذا كتبت الفاتحة

BURSEVI:v5p150/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p150/r2.claim: People should cling to the Qur'an for healing; it identifies sins as disease and repentance as medicine, and one must recognize illness before treating it.
BURSEVI:v5p150/r2.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتمسك بالقرآن ويداوي به مرضه

BURSEVI:v5p150/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p150/r3.claim: When favored with health and abundance, a person turns away from gratitude and arrogantly turns aside; hardship brings despair of God's mercy.
BURSEVI:v5p150/r3.anchor: {وإذآ أنعمنا} (وون أنعام كنيم ما) {على الانسان} بالصحة والسعة

BURSEVI:v5p150/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p150/r4.claim: “Turning aside” is figurative for pride. Assigning favor to God but describing evil as merely touching a person suggests good is intended in itself whereas evil is not; the verse describes some people and does not conflict with another verse about those who pray extensively under hardship.
BURSEVI:v5p150/r4.anchor: فهو كناية عن الاستكبار والتعظم لأن نأي الجانب وتحويل الوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r1.claim: God's favor means health, wealth, and similar gifts; 'the human' can mean the species, so the statement need apply only to some people.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r1.anchor: بالصحة والسعة ونحوهما ( ﴿ على الإنسان ﴾ أي جنسه فيكفي في صحة الحكم وجوده في بعض الأفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r2.claim: Some identify the human here specifically as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد به الوليد بن المغيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r3.claim: When favored, the person turns from remembrance as if self-sufficient and neglects the duties of gratitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r3.anchor: ( أعرض ( عن ذكرنا كأنه مستغن عنا فضلا عن القيام بمواجب شكرنا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r4.claim: Naʾā bi-janibihi depicts turning one's side or back from obedience; its root sense is distance and it makes the aversion vivid.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r4.anchor: لوى عطفه عن طاعتنا وولاها ظهره وأصل معنى النأي البعد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r5.claim: Though near-synonymous with turning away, the phrase may be coordinated to imply nuance and add rhetorical force; the claim that emphasis requires omission of conjunction is not binding.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r5.anchor: ومثله يجوز عطفه لايهام المغايرة بينهما وهو أبلغ من ترك العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r6.claim: The 'side' may be literal, a sign of arrogance, or a metonym for the person himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r6.anchor: والجانب على ظاهره والمراد ترك ذلك ويجوز أن يكون كناية عن الاستكبار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r7.claim: Ibn Amir, in Ibn Dhakwan's transmission, reads nāʾa here and in Fussilat; Al-Alusi discusses metathesis or a sense of rising, haste, or sluggishness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان ( وناء ) هنا وفي فصلت فقيل ذلك من باب القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r8.claim: When hardship touches him, he despairs because he failed to behave well in prosperity and therefore expects no divine grace in adversity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r8.anchor: شديد اليأس من رحمتنا لأنه لم يحسن معاملتنا في الرخاء حتى يرجو فضلنا في الشدة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r9.claim: Attributing blessings to God but merely saying evil touches a person signals that good is intended by divine generosity while evil is not so in itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r9.anchor: وفي إسناد المساس إلى الشر بعد إسناد الانعام إلى ضميره تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r10.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r10.claim: The Prophet's supplication says that good is in God's hands while evil is not attributed to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r10.anchor: اللهم إن الخير بيديك والشر ليس إليك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r11.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r11.claim: Philosophers say God is perfect in power, wisdom, and knowledge; defects and evils arise from limited receptivity in contingent beings, not divine stinginess.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147/r11.anchor: إن الأول تعالى تام القدرة والحكمة والعلم كامل في جميع أفاعيله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r1.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r1.claim: Philosophers distinguish evil as nonbeing, such as poverty or simple ignorance, from positive harms that block possible good.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r1.anchor: أن الشر يطلق عرفا على معنيين أحدهما ما هو عدم كالفقر والجهل البسيط

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r2.claim: Pure lack of existence or perfection that a thing could never possess is one kind of privation; only God has absolute perfection, while contingent beings have degrees of limitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r2.anchor: الأول عدم محض ليس بأزاء الوجود الذي يطلبه طباع الشيء ولا مما يمكن حصوله له من الكمالات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r3.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r3.claim: The source of this unavoidable imperfection is essential contingency, which separates possible beings from necessary existence.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r4.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r4.claim: A second privation is loss of a good or perfection that a thing could attain; this applies to material beings, not immaterial creations made perfect for their kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r4.anchor: والثاني ما يكون عدم ما يطلبه الشيء أو ما يمكن حصوله له من الكمالات ولا يتصور هذا في غير الماديات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r5.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r5.claim: Material receptivity and prime matter explain this second kind of privation, ultimately tracing it to contingency.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r5.anchor: وهذا الشر منبعه الهيولي ومنبعها الإمكان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r6.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r6.claim: A further conventional sense of evil is anything that blocks attainable existence or perfection, such as damaging weather, vice, theft, or pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r6.anchor: وثانيهما ما يمنع الشيء عن الوصول إلى الخير الممكن في حقه من الوجود أو كمال الوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r7.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r7.claim: They call privation true evil and positive harmful things metaphorical evil: if an existent thing is evil, it must deprive itself or another of being or perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r7.anchor: والبرهان عليه أنه لو كان أمرا وجوديا فلا يخلو أما أن يكون شرا لنفسه أو لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r8.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r8.claim: An existent cause is not itself evil if it removes nothing; fire is good for its own perfection though harmful to its victim, while revenge may perfect an irascible faculty.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r8.anchor: وكذا الإحراق كمال للنار وشر لمن يتضرر به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r9.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r9.claim: Thus being as being is good and nonbeing as nonbeing is evil; some essential privations have no cause, while accidental losses require one.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r9.anchor: فالوجود من حيث أنه وجود خير محض والعدم من حيث أنه عدم شر محض

ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r10.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes unavoidable limitations rooted in a thing's essence from losses of additional qualities; the latter, such as lacking philosophy, require explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p147#2/r10.anchor: والكلام ليس في الأول الذي لا لمية له إذ قد تقرر أنه ليس للماهيات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r1.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r1.claim: Evil is rare: what exists is wholly good or has more good than evil; pure evil, dominant evil, or an equal balance does not exist.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r1.anchor: وهذا الشر إنما يوجد يوجد في الأشياء على سبيل الندرة فكل ما وجد فهو خير محض أو خيره أكثر من شره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r2.claim: Since God is pure good, only Magians imagine an independent source of pure evil; withholding pure or predominant good would itself cause greater evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r2.anchor: كما توهمه كفرة المجوس ثم كل ما كان خيرا محضا أو كان خيره أكثر يصدر من الواجب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r3.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r3.claim: The elemental world's rare evils cannot justify withholding abundant goods; these goods enable many beings and are not evil relative to the total order.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r3.anchor: ولا تسوغ عناية المبدع ورحمة الجواد إهماله وإلا لزم خير كثير لشر قليل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r4.claim: A small speck of evil among oceans of good may add beauty to the whole, like a dark beauty mark on a fair face.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r4.anchor: كالشامة السوداء على الصورة المليحة البيضاء يزيدها حسنا وملاحة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r5.claim: This account assumes, as Ashʿaris hold, that divine choice is not equally directed to alternatives without a reason; philosophers say God's choice follows universal laws and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r5.anchor: ولا يخفى أن هذا إنما يتم على القول بأنه تعالى لا يمكن أن تكون إرادته متساوية النسبة إلى الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r6.claim: Al-Alusi calls al-Razi's dismissal of philosophers' inquiry as pointless partisan: serious philosophers affirm divine choice, and their question addresses the problem of evil under a pure-good God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r6.anchor: وقول الإمام : إن الفلاسفة لما قالوا بالإيجاب والجبر في الأفعال فخوضهم في هذا المبحث

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r7.claim: God brings about either things free of evil or things with little evil whose absence would cause much greater evil, and does so when a person's nature seeks them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r7.anchor: ما يصدر عنه تعالى إما ما هو بريء بالكلية عن الشر وإما ما يلزمه شر قليل وفي تركه شر كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r8.claim: Al-Alusi links this principle to 20:50 and says the discussion in al-Isharat and its commentaries is extensive.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p149/r8.anchor: كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى ( أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r6.claim: When God grants a person favor, that person turns away from remembering and calling on God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r7.claim: Naʾā bijānibihi means he distances himself, leaving closeness to God through prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r7.anchor: {ونأى بجانبه} أي تباعد عنا بنفسه أي ترك التقرب إلى الله بالدعاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r8.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r8.claim: Ata explains the phrase as becoming arrogant and haughty.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r9.claim: Readers vary the vowels in naʾā; Ibn Amir and Abu Jaʿfar read nāʾa like jāʾa, with one view treating it as equivalent to naʾā and another deriving it from rising.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر "وناء" مثل جاء قيل: هو بمعنى نأى وقيل: ناء من النوء وهو النهوض والقيام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r1.claim: Al-sharr here means hardship and harm; yaʾūsan means despairing and hopeless.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r1.anchor: {وإذا مسه الشر} الشدة والضرر {كان يئوسا} أي آيسا قنوطا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r2.claim: Another reading is that a person prays in distress, but despairs if the answer is delayed; believers should keep praying rather than despair when the answer is late.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p123#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه يتضرع ويدعو عند الضر والشدة فإذا تأخرت الإجابة يئس

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r4.claim: When given health and abundance, a person turns away from remembering God and distances himself with an arrogant, self-sufficient air.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r4.anchor: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسن } بالصحة والسعة { أعرض } عن ذكر الله. { ونأى بجانبه } لوى عطفه وبعد بنفسه عنه كأنه مستغن مستبد بأمره،

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r5.claim: Turning one's flank away may be a metaphor for pride, as that is a custom of the arrogant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كناية عن الاستكبار لأنه من عادة المستكبرين

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, through Ibn Dhakwān, reads وناء here and in Fuṣṣilat, either by metathesis or with the sense 'he rose.'
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان هنا وفي «فصلت» { وناء } على القلب أو على أنه بمعنى نهض.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r7.claim: When struck by illness or poverty, a person despairs intensely of God's relief.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:82-83/r7.anchor: وإذا مسه الشر } من مرض أو فقر. { كان يئوسا } شديد اليأس من روح الله

QASHANI:17:83/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:83/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:83/r1.claim: At blessings, a person fixed on self and body sees only immediate material effects, grows proud, and turns away from the Real.
QASHANI:17:83/r1.anchor: لوقوفه مع النفس والبدن وكون القوى البدنية متناهية لا تتدبر الأمور الغير المتناهية

QASHANI:17:83/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:83/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:83/r2.claim: At harm, a person despairs because the veil hides the all-powerful God; insight would recognize God's power in both states.
QASHANI:17:83/r2.anchor: وكذا في جانب الشر إذا مسه يئس لاحتجابه عن القادر وقدرته

QASHANI:17:83/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:83/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:83/r3.claim: The discerning response is gratitude, which binds blessings, and patience, which repels calamities: thank the Giver without arrogance or forgetfulness, and hope for relief without despair.
QASHANI:17:83/r3.anchor: وفي الثانية أن الصبر دفاع النقم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r8.claim: When blessed, the generic human turns away proudly from the giver.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r8.anchor: أي عن ذكر المنعم كإعراض هؤلاء عند مجيء هذه النعمة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r9.claim: The human turns away in pride and blindness, then despairs when touched by harm, except those God preserves from the devil’s power.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r9.anchor: أي تباعد تكبرا { بجانبه } بطرا وعمى عن الحقائق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r10.claim: When harmed, the generic human becomes deeply hopeless and distrustful of God’s mercy, except those He preserves.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p418/r10.anchor: أي شديد اليأس هلعا وقلة ثقة بما عنده من رحمة الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r1.claim: The apparent generalization about human ingratitude is restricted to the prodigal in 10:12 and balanced by the patient in 11:11; the author says these exceptions are few.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r1.anchor: بأن هذا في المسرفين دون غيرهم , وبقوله تعالى في سورة هود

DURR-FULL:v5p330/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses turning aside as distancing oneself from them.
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ونأى بجانبه} قال: تباعد منا

DURR-FULL:v5p330/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses despair as hopelessness and one's manner as one's direction or way.
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {كان يؤوسا} قال: قنوطا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r1.claim: جانب means flank or side; the bāʾ marks accompaniment, and moving one’s side away depicts recoil from something.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r1.anchor: والجانب : الجنب . وهو الجهة من الجسد التي فيها اليد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r2.claim: The phrase نأى بجانبه adds distancing and recoil beyond the meaning of أعرض; the rejected person turns away from worship and gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r2.anchor: فالمفاد من قوله : { وناء بجانبه } صد عن العبادة والشكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r3.claim: The object of turning away is omitted because context supplies it: the person turns away from God, worship, commands, and prohibitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r3.anchor: وحذف متعلق { أعرض ونأى } لدلالة المقام عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r4.claim: The majority read وناء with hamza after nūn and alif after the hamza.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { وناء } بهمزة بعد النون وألف بعد الهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r5.speaker: ابن ذكوان، أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r5.claim: Ibn Amir in Ibn Dhakwan’s transmission and Abu Jaafar read the letters in reversed order; this metathesis eases a hamza after a consonant followed by a long vowel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر في رواية ابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر { وناء } بألف بعد النون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r6.claim: An alternative explanation takes ناء in that reading to mean becoming heavy with respect to gratitude, as in the parable of one who clings to the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r6.anchor: وقيل : ناء في هذه القراءة بمعنى ثقل ، أي عن الشكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r7.claim: The distress clause prevents the inference that losing blessings reforms the person: in hardship he despairs, remains angry and constricted, and does not repent; this does not conflict with 41:51.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r7.anchor: وجملة وإذا مسه الشر كان يؤسا احتراس من أن يتوهم السامع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r8.claim: يؤسا is an intensive form, and كان conveys entrenched despair; the response is striking because hardship should prompt reflection on ways to remedy it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p192/r8.anchor: ودل قوله : كان يؤسا } على قوة يأسه إذ صيغ له مثال المبالغة

SULAMI:v1p395#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p395#2/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says people turn from the Giver through blessings by savoring obedience, enjoying or settling into it, or relying on it for protection; the greatest blessings are guidance, faith, gnosis, and divine friendship.
SULAMI:v1p395#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : أعرض بالنعمة عن المنعم والنعمة العظمى الهداية والإيمان والمعرفة والولاية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r5.claim: The human may mean unbelievers in particular, using universal phrasing rhetorically; the preceding reference to wrongdoers supports the connection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r5.anchor: الإنسان في هذه الآية لا يراد به العموم، وإنما يراد به بعضه وهم الكفرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r6.claim: Alternatively, humanity generally has this blameworthy trait, strongest in unbelievers and present in sinners too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الإنسان في هذه الآية عاما للجنس، على معنى أن هذا الخلق الذميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r7.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r7.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said of a believer: he turned away, so God turned away from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r7.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مؤمن: «فأعرض فأعرض الله عنه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r8.claim: Aʿraḍa means turning one’s side away and naʾā means moving far off, depicting abandonment of faith and gratitude.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r8.anchor: ومعنى أعرض ولانا عرضه، ونأى أي بعد، وهذه استعارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r9.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAmir alone reads wa-nāʾa; some take it as rising while turned aside, others as a reordered form of naʾā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده «وناء» ، ومعناه نهض أي متباعدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r10.claim: The author distinguishes nāʾa as arrogant self-separation from naʾā, distance and departure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r10.anchor: والذي عندي أن «ناء ونأى» فعلان متباينان، وناء بجانبه عبارة عن التحيز والاستبداد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r11.claim: When illness, financial loss, or other harm touches them, unbelievers despair because they do not believe in God or trust His control of events.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p480/r11.anchor: ثم وصف الكفرة بأنهم إذا مسهم شر من مرض أو مصيبة في مال أو غير ذلك يئسوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r1.claim: “The human” here is the unbeliever, specifically al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس الانسان هاهنا الكافر والمراد به الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r2.claim: The blessing is ample provision and removal of affliction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون وهذا الإنعام سعة الرزق وكشف البلاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read naʾā with fatḥa on nūn and hamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم ونأى على وزن نعى بفتح النون والهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads nāʾa in the pattern of bāʿa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ناء مثل باع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf from Sulaym from Ḥamza read nāʾa with imāla; Khallād from Sulaym transmits naʾi with a broken hamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r5.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وخلف عن سليم عن حمزة وناء باماله النون والهمزة وروى خلاد عن سليم نئي بفتح النون وكسر الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r6.claim: Naʾā bi-jānibihi means he distances himself from fulfilling the rights of blessings; another gloss is that he grows proud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r6.anchor: والمعنى تباعد عن القيام بحقوق النعم وقيل تعظم وتكبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r7.claim: When evil—affliction and poverty—touches a person, he becomes deeply despairing and stops hoping for God’s bounty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p80/r7.anchor: واذا مسه الشر أي نزل به البلاء والفقر كان يؤوسا أي قنوطا شديد اليأس لا يرجو فضل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r1.claim: Human beings generally turn from worship and turn away when God grants wealth, health, provision, victory or what they desire, except those God protects.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r1.anchor: إذا أنعم الله عليه بمال وعافية، وفتح ورزق ونصر، ونال ما يريد، أعرض عن طاعة الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses turning aside as moving away from God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r3.claim: When hardship and calamities touch a person, he despairs of future good; Ibn Kathir links this to the contrast in Hud 10–11 between boastful joy and the patience of the righteous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113/r3.anchor: وبأنه إذا مسه الشر -وهو المصائب والحوادث والنوائب - {كان يئوسا} أي: قنط أن يعود يحصل له

JISHUMI:v6p4286/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r9.claim: Na'y means distance or turning away; ya's means despair and is synonymous with qunut.
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r9.anchor: والنأي: البعد، نأى ينأى نأيا بعد. واليأس ضد الرجاء، ونظيره: القنوط

JISHUMI:v6p4286/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r12.claim: Ya'usa is accusative because it is the predicate of kana.
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r12.anchor: يئوسا نصب؛ لأنه خبر (كان)، تقديره: كان الإنسان يؤوسا.

JISHUMI:v6p4286/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r13.claim: The composition asks how human turning away after receiving favor connects to the preceding discussion of the Qur'an.
JISHUMI:v6p4286/r13.anchor: يقال: كيف اتصل قوله: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان بما قبله من ذكر القرآن؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r1.claim: When given health and prosperity, a person turns from remembering God as if self-sufficient; turning one's side intensifies the image of arrogance and rejection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r1.anchor: بالصحة والسعة { أعرض } عن ذكر الله ، كأنه مستغن عنه مستبد بنفسه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r2.claim: When hardship such as poverty, illness, or calamity touches him, he becomes deeply despairing of God's relief.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r2.anchor: من فقر أو مرض أو نازلة من النوازل { كان } شديد اليأس من روح الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r3.claim: The reading wa-nāʾa bi-jānibihi reverses the positions of the root's lām and ʿayn, like rāʾ in raʾā; it can also derive from nāʾ meaning to rise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p644#2/r3.anchor: وقرىء ( وناء بجانبه ) بتقديم اللام على العين ، كقوله ( راء ) في ( رأى ) ويجوز أن يكون من ( ناء ) بمعنى ( نهض

FARRA:v2p129/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p129/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p129/r5.claim: When hamza is dropped from يؤوسا, Arabic allows adjacent silent letters; readers instead move the vowel onto wāw, which Farra says is heavier and unattested in ordinary speech.
FARRA:v2p129/r5.anchor: فإن العرب تقول يوسا ويووسا تجمعون بين ساكنين

FARRA:v2p129/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p129/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p129/r6.claim: He compares the same treatment with ولا يؤده حفظهما and بعذاب بئيس, where readers move the vowel but Arabic speech retains hamza-less clusters.
FARRA:v2p129/r6.anchor: فهذا كلام العرب: والقراء يقولون (يووسا) و (يووده) فيحركون الواو إلى الرفع

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r1.claim: When blessed with health and wealth, a person turns away and distances himself from goodness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r1.anchor: إذا أنعمنا عليه بالصحة والغنى أعرض ونأى وبعد من الخير

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r2.claim: Alternatively, when given guidance, a person turns away from listening and distances himself from acceptance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r2.anchor: إذا أنعمنا عليه بالهداية أعرض عن السماع وبعد من القبول

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r3.claim: Nāʾā bi-jānibihi may describe self-admiration, since the conceited shuns people and keeps away from them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r3.anchor: أعجب بنفسه , لأن المعجب نافر من الناس متباعد عنهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r4.claim: It may instead mean distancing oneself from one's Lord.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r5.claim: Despair of relief after hardship may come from denial and disbelief.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r6.claim: Alternatively, one despairs because one knows one's sin will bring punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r6.anchor: بعلمه بمعصيته أنه معاقب على ذنبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r7.claim: The affliction here may be poverty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p268/r9.claim: It may also be the sword.

MUJAHID:v1p368#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p368#2/r1.speaker: author
MUJAHID:v1p368#2/r1.claim: Turning away and leaning aside means becoming distant from Us.
MUJAHID:v1p368#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ أعرض ونأى بجانبه ﴾ يقول تباعد منا

MUQATIL:17:83-84/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:83-84/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:83-84/r1.claim: The human is an unbeliever: when given provision he turns from supplication and withdraws; when poverty touches him he despairs of good.
MUQATIL:17:83-84/r1.anchor: { وإذآ أنعمنا على الإنسان } ، يعني الكافر بالخير، يعني الرزق، { أعرض } عن الدعاء، { ونأى بجانبه } ، يقول: وتباعد بجانبه،

MUQATIL:17:83-84/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:83-84/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:83-84/r2.claim: The adversity is poverty; when it touches him, he despairs of good.
MUQATIL:17:83-84/r2.anchor: { وإذا مسه الشر } ، يعني وإذا أصابه الفقر، { كان يئوسا } [آية: 83]، يعني آيسا من الخير.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r1.claim: God's favor may mean health and prosperity, or the Qurʾān; in either case the person turns away from remembrance or from the Qurʾān.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان ﴾ بالصحة والسعة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r2.claim: Naʾā bijānibihi reinforces turning away: one turns the face's side away and then the back, or the phrase indicates the arrogance typical of the proud.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r2.anchor: ﴿ ونأى بجانبه ﴾ تأكيد للاعراض لأن الاعراض عن الشيء أن يوليه عرض وجهه والنأي بالجانب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r3.claim: Ḥamza reads the verb with imāla and ʿAlī with kasra.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r4.claim: The affliction may be poverty or illness, or any severe event; the person then becomes intensely despairing of God's relief.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p297#5/r4.anchor: ﴿ وإذا مسه الشر ﴾ الفقر والمرض أو نازلة من النوازل ﴿ كان يؤوسا ﴾ شديد اليأس من روح الله

QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r1.claim: The people whom Qurʾān increases in loss turn from reflecting on God's signs and are ungrateful for His blessings; one report says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r1.anchor: أي هؤلاء الذين يزيدهم القرآن خسارا صفتهم الإعراض عن تدبر آيات الله

QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r2.claim: To turn one's side away means arrogance and distance from fulfilling God's rights; the root denotes being far away, with related forms for making distant or moving apart.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r3.speaker: النابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r3.claim: Al-Nabigha's line uses al-muntaʾā for a far-off place, illustrating the root's sense of distance.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r4.claim: Ibn Amir, in Ibn Dhakwan's transmission, reads nāʾa with the hamza delayed, a metathesis of naʾā like raʾā and rāʾa; other readings are nuiʾa and the majority naʾā.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر في رواية ابن ذكوان «ناء» مثل

QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r5.claim: A further derivation connects the form to nawʾ, rising or standing, though the word may also mean falling or sitting as an antonym.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو من النوء وهو النهوض والقيام.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r6.claim: When poverty, illness, or hardship touches such a person, he despairs because he does not trust God's grace.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:83/r6.anchor: أي إذا ناله شدة من فقر أو سقم أو بؤس يئس وقنط

MAJAZ:v1p389/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p389/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p389/r3.claim: نأى بجانبه means he turned away and withdrew to his side.

MAJAZ:v1p389/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p389/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p389/r4.claim: يؤسا means profoundly despairing and without hope.
MAJAZ:v1p389/r4.anchor: «وإذا مسه الشر كان يؤسا» (83) أي قنوطا، أي شديد اليأس لا يرجو

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies “the human” as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; al-Rāzī calls this interpretation far-fetched.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إن الإنسان ها هنا هو الوليد بن المغيرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī instead reads the verse generally: people tend to become arrogant, forget servitude, and rebel against God when they obtain what they want, as 96:6–7 says.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r2.anchor: المراد أن نوع الإنسان من شأنه أنه إذا فاز بمقصوده ووصل إلى مطلوبه

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r3.claim: Aʿraḍa means he turned away, literally turning his face aside; naʾā bi-jānibihi means he moved far away.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r3.anchor: قوله أعرض أي ولى ظهره أي عرضه إلى ناحية ونأى بجانبه أي تباعد

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r4.claim: Moving one’s flank away is an idiom for arrogance, since the arrogant customarily turn aside and present their backs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r4.anchor: والنأي بالجانب أن يلوي عنه عطفه ويوليه ظهره وأراد الاستكبار

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r5.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on both nūn and hamza in naʾā; it is the dominant Arabic form and also occurs in Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r5.anchor: قراءة العامة بفتح النون والهمزة وفي حم السجدة مثله

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads nāʾ; it can reflect metathesis of the word’s final and middle radicals, as in rāʾ for raʾā, or derive from a verb meaning to rise.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r6.anchor: قراءة ابن عامر ناء وله وجهان تقديم اللام على العين كقولهم راء في رأى

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī incline both fatḥas: they incline the hamza and then give the nūn kasra by assimilation to that vowel.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r7.anchor: قراءة حمزة والكسائي بإمالة الفتحتين وذلك لأنهم أمالوا الهمزة من نأى

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim in Abū Bakr’s narration, and Naṣīr from al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza read naʾā with an open nūn and kasra on the hamza, inclining the hamza.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر ونصير عن الكسائي وحمزة نأى بفتح النون

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r9.claim: The evil that touches a person includes poverty, sickness, or any calamity; then he is intensely despairing of God’s mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r9.anchor: إذا مسه فقر أو مرض أو نازلة من النوازل كان يؤوسا شديد اليأس من رحمة الله

RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r10.claim: The person who prospers forgets God, while the deprived person is consumed by grief and also fails to remember God; al-Rāzī compares the pattern with 89:15–16 and 70:19–21.
RAZI-FULL:v21p29/r10.anchor: إن فاز بالنعمة والدولة اغتر بها فنسي ذكر الله ، وإن بقي في الحرمان عن الدنيا

NAHHAS:v2p437/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p437/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p437/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads وناء بجانبه; al-Kisāʾī says the forms are dialects, and al-Farrāʾ assigns نأى to the Ḥijāz and ناء to some Hawāzin, Kināna, and most Anṣār.
NAHHAS:v2p437/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي هما لغتان . وقال الفراء : لغة أهل الحجاز نأى

NAHHAS:v2p437/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p437/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p437/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says ناء is metathesized from نأى; the forms نأيت and رأيت show the original order, unlike hypothetical نئت and رئت.
NAHHAS:v2p437/r5.anchor: والدليل على أنه مقلوب أنهم قد أجمعوا على أن يقولوا : نأيت نأيا

NAHHAS:v2p437/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p437/r6.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p437/r6.claim: For easing the hamza in يؤوسا, al-Kisāʾī transmits يوسا and also cites وإذا المودة, comparing its pronunciation to الموزة.
NAHHAS:v2p437/r6.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن العرب الحذف ' كان يوسا '

STUDYQURAN:17:83/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r1.claim: Human life varies as a spiritual and moral test: God tests people with evil and good, but people often fail it.
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r1.anchor: The Quran presents the vagaries of human existence as a spiritual and moral test, since God tries people with evil and with good

STUDYQURAN:17:83/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r2.claim: People often meet blessings with disdain, arrogance, and self-satisfaction instead of gratitude, though every blessing comes from God.
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r2.anchor: human beings often fail the test, responding to “blessing” with disdain

STUDYQURAN:17:83/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r3.claim: People despair and become anxious in hardship, sometimes invoking God and then forgetting Him when hardship passes.
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r3.anchor: When evil befalls human beings, they are given to despair

STUDYQURAN:17:83/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r4.claim: The right response to affliction is patient endurance and affirming that people belong to God and return to Him.
STUDYQURAN:17:83/r4.anchor: Their response, however, should be to bear their affliction with patience

TAB-FULL:v15p64/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r1.claim: After rescue from the sea's danger to shore, a person turns from God's remembrance despite having called on Him alone in distress, acting as if he had never prayed.
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r1.anchor: فنجيناه من رب ما هو فيه في البحر، وهو ما قد أشرف فيه عليه من الهلاك بعصوف الريح عليه إلى البر،

TAB-FULL:v15p64/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r2.claim: Naya bi-janibihi means he turns away from God with his own person, as though he had not previously called on Him in hardship.
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r2.anchor: يقول: وبعد منا بجانبه، يعني بنفسه، كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه قبل ذلك،

TAB-FULL:v15p64/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r3.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as moving far away from God.
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ونأى بجانبه} [الإسراء: 83] قال: تباعد منا

TAB-FULL:v15p64/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the eloquent reading with the hamza before the alif; the Medinan reading placing it after the alif is valid Arabic metathesis but less eloquent.
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r4.anchor: والقراءة على تصيير الهمزة في نأى قبل الألف، وهي اللغة الفصيحة، وبها نقرأ.

TAB-FULL:v15p64/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r5.claim: The Medinan reading ناء shifts the hamza as Arabs do in related forms, but it is not the more eloquent language; cited examples illustrate the shift.
TAB-FULL:v15p64/r5.anchor: وكان بعض أهل المدينة يقرأ ذلك (وناء) فيصير الهمزة بعد الألف، وذلك وإن كان لغة جائزة قد جاءت عن العرب

TABATABAI:17:82-100/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r1.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r1.claim: Al-Raghib explains that aʿraḍa ʿannī means turning away while showing one's side; naʾā bi-janibihi means taking distance from God.
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r1.anchor: وإذا قيل أعرض عني فمعناه ولى مبديا عرضه

TABATABAI:17:82-100/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r2.claim: Together, “turned away and kept his side distant” pictures a person's separation from God when blessed; some commentators also read it as arrogance and self-exaltation.
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r2.anchor: يمثل حال الإنسان في تباعده وانقطاعه من ربه عندما ينعم عليه

TABATABAI:17:82-100/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r3.claim: When even slight harm touches a person, he despairs of good; evil is not directly attributed to God because it is relative to its bearer, while the universal order makes it incidental to greater good.
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r3.anchor: ولم ينسب الشر إليه تعالى كما نسب النعمة تنزيها له تعالى

TABATABAI:17:82-100/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r4.claim: Ordinary people attach to visible causes during prosperity and forget gratitude; when harm removes those causes, they despair because they see no other source of good.
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r4.anchor: اشتغل بظواهر الأسباب وأخلد إليها فنسينا فلم يذكرنا ولم يشكرنا

TABATABAI:17:82-100/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r5.claim: This describes the socially conditioned person's ordinary state, unlike the innate or emergency state in which distress makes people forget apparent causes and turn back to God.
TABATABAI:17:82-100/r5.anchor: فللإنسان حالان حال فطرية تهديه إلى الرجوع إلى ربه عند مس الضر ونزول الشر وحال عاديه

TABATABAI:17:82#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r1.claim: There is no contradiction with verses where distress makes people turn to God: those describe the innate response when apparent causes fail, whereas 17:83 describes ordinary attachment to causes.
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r1.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن لا منافاة بين هذه الآية والآيات الدالة على أن الإنسان إذا مسه الضر رجع إلى ربه

TABATABAI:17:82#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r2.claim: The verse follows the Qur'an's warning of increased loss by explaining that people forget God amid blessings and despair at harm.
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r2.anchor: ويظهر أيضا وجه اتصال الآية بما قبلها وأنها متصلة بالآية السابقة من جهة ذيلها

TABATABAI:17:82#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r3.speaker: أفلاطون
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r3.claim: Plato's account treats evil as privation: in killing, the evil is the victim's loss of life, not the swordsman's strength, the sharp blade, or the victim's capacity to be cut.
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r3.anchor: نقل عن أفلاطون أن الشر عدم وقد بين ذلك بالأمثلة

TABATABAI:17:82#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r4.claim: Cosmic evils are privations attached to events and thus have a share in occurrence; they relate to divine decree incidentally, not essentially.
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r4.anchor: كانت أعداما مضافة لا عدما مطلقا فلها حظ من الوجود والوقوع

TABATABAI:17:82#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r5.claim: Absolute nonexistence is one kind of nonbeing; privation is a missing perfection in something suited to possess it, such as blindness in a being naturally capable of sight.
TABATABAI:17:82#4/r5.anchor: وإما مضاف إلى ملكة وهو عدم كمال الوجود عما من شأنه ذلك

TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r1.claim: A thing's lacking another possible essence, such as a plant lacking animal life, follows from essences and is not something created; privative defects such as illness and pain arise only in material things from limited capacity.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r1.anchor: وهذا النوع من العدم من لوازم الماهيات وهي اعتبارية غير مجعولة

TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r2.claim: God's decree essentially wills the existence a thing can receive; the accompanying lack is due to incapacity or limited receptivity and is attributed to creation only incidentally.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r2.anchor: فالذي تعلقت به كلمة الإيجاد والإرادة الإلهية وشمله القضاء بالذات

TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r3.claim: Of five possible balances of good and evil, pure evil, evil-dominant, and equal cases do not occur; divine wisdom creates pure good and what has more good than evil, since omitting them would yield greater evil.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r3.anchor: ولا يوجد شيء من الثلاثة الأخيرة لاستلزامه الترجيح من غير مرجح أو ترجيح المرجوح على الراجح

TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r4.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi says this discussion has no place for philosophers who treat God as a necessary cause rather than a voluntary agent; the author replies that necessity belongs to the effect and cannot compel its cause.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r4.anchor: وعن الإمام الرازي أنه لا محل لهذا البحث منهم بناء على ما ذهبوا إليه من كونه تعالى علة تامة

TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r5.speaker: صاحب روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r5.claim: The author praises al-Alusi's fair account: the debate assumes whether God's will is indifferent between opposites, while philosophers say divine choice follows universal laws, wisdom, and visible or hidden interests.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#2/r5.anchor: ولقد أنصف صاحب روح المعاني حيث أشار أولا إلى نظير ما تقدم من البحث

TABATABAI:17:84/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:84/r1.speaker: الإمام
TABATABAI:17:84/r1.claim: The quoted criticism says philosophers' discussion of evil is pointless because they posit necessary compulsion in divine acts, like fire necessarily burning; the author calls this biased because philosophers affirm choice and investigate evil to avoid positing two principles.
TABATABAI:17:84/r1.anchor: إن الفلاسفة لما قالوا بالإيجاب والجبر في الأفعال فخوضهم في هذا المبحث من جملة الفضول والضلال

TABATABAI:17:84/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:84/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:84/r2.claim: The author says the criticism is biased: philosophers affirm divine choice, and examine how evil occurs because God is pure good and they must avoid the dualist claim of separate good and evil principles.
TABATABAI:17:84/r2.anchor: ناش من التعصب لأن محققيهم يثبتون الاختيار

TABRISI:17:82/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:82/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:82/r1.claim: Readings of naʾā vary: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn ʿĀmir via Ibn Dhakwān lengthen and hamzate it; some transmitters use naʾi with a fatḥa then kasra, Ḥamza via al-ʿAjalī, Khalaf, and al-Kisāʾī use kasra on both, and the rest read naʾā.
TABRISI:17:82/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان وناء بجانبه ممدودة مهموزة

TABRISI:17:82/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:82/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:17:82/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī analyzes nāʾ as an inverted fāʿil form and cites a poem using rāʾanī as evidence.
TABRISI:17:82/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي ناء مثل فاع وهو على القلب وتقديره فلع

TABRISI:17:82/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:82/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:82/r3.claim: Imāla follows because the alif derives from yāʾ in naʾy; readers may incline the first vowel toward the second, while others leave it open.
TABRISI:17:82/r3.anchor: ومن أمال الفتحتين فلأن الألف منقلبة من الياء التي في النأي

TABRISI:17:83/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:83/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:83/r1.claim: The statement that supplication only drove them farther away echoes Noah 71:6; alternatively, the Qurʾān exposes their hidden malice and plots against the Prophet.

TABRISI:17:83/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:83/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:83/r2.claim: When granted blessings, a person turns from remembrance as if never to have prayed, then distances himself from gratitude and the duties owed for the blessing.
TABRISI:17:83/r2.anchor: أي ولى كأنه لم يقبل علينا بالدعاء والابتهال

TABRISI:17:83/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:83/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:17:83/r3.claim: Mujāhid reads distancing himself as turning away from God, implying arrogance, self-exaltation, and conceit.
TABRISI:17:83/r3.anchor: معناه تباعد منا وعلى هذا فيكون معناه تجبر وتكبر

TABRISI:17:83/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:83/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:83/r4.claim: When hardship, poverty, or affliction strikes, the person despairs instead of patiently hoping for relief, unlike a believer who hopes for relief and mercy.
TABRISI:17:83/r4.anchor: وإذا أصابه المحنة والشدة والفقر لم يصبر وكان قنوطا

TABRISI:17:83/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:83/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:83/r5.claim: Although phrased generally, the description specifically concerns unbelievers, who expect no reward for illness and recoil from it; afflictions are truly wise and right.
TABRISI:17:83/r5.anchor: فيكون المراد بالآية خاصا وإن كان اللفظ عاما

THALABI:v6p129/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p129/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p129/r3.claim: When given blessing, a person turns from remembrance and withdraws; when harm touches him, he despairs.
THALABI:v6p129/r3.anchor: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض عن ذكرنا ونأى بجانبه وتباعدنا بنفسه

THALABI:v6p129/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p129/r4.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v6p129/r4.claim: Ata interprets turning away as becoming arrogant and proud.

THALABI:v6p129/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p129/r5.speaker: القراء
THALABI:v6p129/r5.claim: Readers differ on the pronunciation of “ونأى”: Abu Amr, Asim, Nafi, and Hamza in some transmissions use imāla; al-Kisai, Khalaf, and other transmissions of Hamza use kasra; most use fatḥa on both vowels.
THALABI:v6p129/r5.anchor: واختلف القراء في هذا الحديث، فقرأ أبو عمر وعاصم ونافع وحمزة في بعض الروايات عنهم

THALABI:v6p129/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p129/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر وعامر
THALABI:v6p129/r6.claim: They read it with the nūn form, explained either as a reversal of “نأى” or as deriving from “النوء,” which can mean rising or falling.
THALABI:v6p129/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعامر: بالنون ولها وجهان: أحدهما: مقلوبة من نأي

THALABI:v6p129/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p129/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p129/r7.claim: “Harm” means hardship and distress; the person becomes hopeless and despairing.
THALABI:v6p129/r7.anchor: وإذا مسه الشر الشدة والضر كان يؤسا قنوطا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the human as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; in prosperity he turns aside instead of praying and imploring as he does in affliction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الوليد بن المغيرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r2.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas gloss naʾa bi-janibihi as distancing himself; a report from Mujahid says he moves away from Us, while Ata says it means acting proudly and arrogantly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r3.claim: The semanticists say he distances himself from fulfilling the rights due for God's blessings; naʾa means distance, as in 6:26, and adds stronger withdrawal to aʿrada.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: بعد نفسه عن القيام بحقوق نعم الله -عز وجل-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r4.claim: The common reading has naʾa with two fatḥas; Ibn Amir reads naʾa with an inverted hamza, like baʿa, a reversal also seen in raʾa/waraʾa and supported by poetry and Abu Ubayda's note.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p454/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read with imala on both fatḥas because the alif derives from the yāʾ of naʾy; Khallad does not incline the nun, while another reading has a kasra on the hamza.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r1.claim: The person meant is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; when favored he ignores supplication rather than praying fervently as in hardship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r1.anchor: { وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان } يريد: الوليد بن المغيرة { أعرض } عن الدعاء والابتهال، فلا يبتهل كابتهاله في البلاء والمحنة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r2.claim: Turning aside means withdrawing from fulfilling the rights due for God's blessings.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r2.anchor: { ونأى بجانبه } بعد بنفسه عن القيام بحقوق نعم الله تعالى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r3.claim: The harm is illness or poverty; ya'us means despairing of good and God's mercy because he does not trust God's grace toward His servants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:83/r3.anchor: { وإذا مسه الشر } أصابه المرض والفقر { كان يؤسا } يائسا عن الخير ومن رحمة الله سبحانه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r4.claim: The human in this example is a polytheist whom God has granted ease and health.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r4.anchor: قوله: {وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان} [الإسراء: 83] ، يعني: المشرك، أعطيناه السعة والعافية.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r5.claim: The favored person turns away from God.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r6.claim: Mujahid explains naʾā bijānibihi as distancing himself from Us; Yahya says it amounts to the same meaning as turning away.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r6.anchor: {ونأى بجانبه} [الإسراء: 83] وقال مجاهد: تباعد منا. وهو واحد.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r7.claim: The harm that touches him consists of illnesses and hardships.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r8.claim: Qatada glosses yaʾūs as despairing and losing hope.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r9.claim: Yahya says he gives up hope of relief because he has no intention of seeking recompense and no hope.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p158/r9.anchor: قال يحيى: يقول: يئس أن يفرج ذلك عنه؛ لأنه ليست له نية ولا حسبة ولا رجاء.

ELMALILI:17:80-84/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:80-84/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:80-84/r10.claim: The ungrateful person turns away and withdraws arrogantly when blessed, then falls into extreme despair when harmed; the righteous response is gratitude in ease and hope and prayer in hardship.
ELMALILI:17:80-84/r10.anchor: nimet hâlinde şükür, şer hâlinde ümit ve dua hasleti bulunmayan insanlardır ki o zâlimlerdir

ELMALILI:17:80-84/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:80-84/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:80-84/r11.claim: Such people are not guided by glad tidings or warnings.
ELMALILI:17:80-84/r11.anchor: Böyleleri tebşir ile de yola gelmez, inzar ile de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r1.claim: “The human” here means the disbelievers previously called zalimun, not all people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r1.anchor: “İnsan”dan maksat, bütün insanlar olmayıp önceki âyette “zalimler” diye tanımlanan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r2.claim: When these disbelievers receive blessings they turn away, fail to acknowledge God as their source, and remain ungrateful; when trouble strikes they sink into pain and grief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r2.anchor: nimetin asıl sahibi olarak Allah’ı bilip O’na şükretmezler, nankörlüklerine devam ederler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s healing and merciful teaching calls for gratitude in speech and action during blessings, and patience, prayer, and seeking God’s help in hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r3.anchor: Allah nimetler verdiğinde insanın sözü ve eylemleriyle O’na şükretmesi, sıkıntı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r4.claim: This response matters religiously and psychologically and morally, as a need of human nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:83/r4.anchor: yalnız dinî bakımdan değil, psikolojik ve moral bakımından da önemlidir

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r1.claim: The common reading places hamza before the weak letter, deriving ونأى from ‘be distant.’
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بتقديم الهمزة على حرف العلة من النأي وهو البعد.

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r2.speaker: ابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r2.claim: Ibn Dhakwan, or Ibn ‘Amir according to the Sheikh, reads ناء with alif before hamza; it can derive from ‘rise.’
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r2.anchor: وابن ذكوان - ونقلها الشيخ عن ابن عامر بكماله-: " ناء " بتقديم الألف على الهمزة.

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r3.claim: The quoted verse uses ناء to mean that a shoulder rose or stood up.
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r3.anchor:
3101- حتى إذا ما التأمت مفاصله
وناء في شق الشمال كاهله

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r4.claim: Another parse treats ناء as metathesis from نأى, like رأى/راء; the author prefers avoiding metathesis when possible.
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنه مقلوب من نأى، ووزنه فلع كقولهم في " رأى " راء، إلى غير ذلك، ولكن متى أمكن عدم القلب فهو أولى.

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r5.claim: The same reading dispute occurs in the sura called Ha Mim al-Sajdah.
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r5.anchor: وهذا الخلاف جار أيضا في سورة حم السجدة.

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r6.speaker: الأخوان وأبو بكر عن عاصم والسوسي
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r6.claim: Al-Akhawan and Abu Bakr from ‘Asim use full imala; al-Susi has an intermediate pronunciation with disagreement.
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r6.anchor: وأمال الألف إمالة محضة الأخوان وأبو بكر عن عاصم، وبين بين بخلاف عنه السوسي،

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r7.claim: The same imala applies in Fussilat, except Abu Bakr does not use it there.
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r7.anchor: وكذلك في فصلت، إلا أبا بكر فإنه لم يمله.

SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r8.speaker: خلف
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r8.claim: Khalaf, Abu al-Harith, and al-Duri from al-Kisa’i incline the nūn fatḥa in both suras.
SAMIN-DURR:17:83/r8.anchor: وأمال فتحة النون في السورتين خلف، وأبو الحارث والدوري عن الكسائي.

ASAD-NOTES:17:82#n99/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:82#n99/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:82#n99/r1.claim: Asad connects this description of human response to blessing and hardship with 11:9-10.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r1.claim: They read naʾā with both nūn and hamza open, in the pattern of naʿā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع: (ونأى بجانبه) في وزن نعى حيث وقع بفتح النون والهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads nāʾa, like bāʿa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده: (وناء بجانبه) مثل باع

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r3.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī have a transmitted form with imāla of the nūn and a kasra on the hamza; another transmission opens the nūn and keeps the hamza kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (وناي) في رواية خلف عن سليم بإمالة النون وكسر الهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r4.claim: Abū Bakr reports a kasra in this verse, while the hamza is open in al-Sajda.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r4.anchor: واختلف عن عاصم فروى أبو بكر أنه كسر هذه التي في سورة بني إسرائيل وفتح الهمزة في السجدة [51]

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r5.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r5.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم أنه فتحهما جميعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r6.claim: Al-Yazīdī and ʿAbd al-Wārith report an open hamza here and in al-Sajda; ʿAbbās reports an imāla-like form glossed as turning aside.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r6.anchor: وأما أبو عمرو فروى عنه اليزيدي: (ونأى) مفتوحة الهمزة هاهنا وفي السجدة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r7.claim: Leaving both fatḥas without imāla is a common Hijazi usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r7.anchor: وترك الإمالة كثير سائغ، وهو قول أهل الحجاز

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir's form is metathesis; the author compares rāʾa and raʾā and cites a poetic witness.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r8.anchor: وهذا على القلب، وتقديره فلع، ومثل هذا في القلب قولهم راء، ورأى

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r9.claim: Imāla of the hamza vowel reflects an underlying yāʾ; imāla of the nūn vowel follows it, since speakers may treat a vowel like a letter and incline one vowel because of another.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r9.anchor: أمال فتحة الهمزة لأن الألف منقلبة من الياء التي في النأي

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r10.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r10.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r10.claim: A form with open nūn and kasra hamza leaves the first vowel uninclined, just as an alif is not inclined merely because of a following alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r10.anchor: أنه لم يمل الفتحة الأولى لإمالة الفتحة الثانية

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r11.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r11.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r11.claim: If Abū Bakr's report means kasra on the nūn without hamza imāla, it follows the present-tense pattern yanʾā, by analogy with verbs such as shahida and abā yaʾbā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p115#2/r11.anchor: وهذا كقول من قال: رأى القمر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r2.claim: Opening nūn and hamza in naʾā preserves the root’s original form, naʾā, on faʿala; the word means to move away.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r2.anchor: أنه أتى بالكلمة على أصلها لأنها في حقيقة اللفظ نأي على وزن فعل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r3.claim: Kasra on both nūn and hamza signals the underlying yāʾ by imālah; neighboring vowels draw each other toward kasra, as in shaʿīr and baʿīr.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r3.anchor: أنه أمال الياء للدلالة عليها فكسر لها الهمزة ليقر بها منها بالمجاورة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r4.claim: Opening nūn but making hamza kasra keeps nūn original and brings hamza toward the neighboring yāʾ; all these forms mean distance, and the noun is al-naʾy.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r4.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح النون أنه بقاها على أصلها وكسر الهمزة لمجاورة الياء

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r5.claim: Postponing hamza with a lengthened vowel derives nāʾa yanūʾu, to rise while bearing a heavy load; its original wāw became alif, as in the verse about a band of men.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p220/r5.anchor: أنه أراد معنى ناء ينوء إذا نهض بثقل مطيقا لحمله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p383/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p383/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p383/r5.claim: The readings of wa-naʾā differ in vowel quality and length: Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ open, Ibn ʿĀmir lengthens, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza transmissions vary, and ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr reports differ between this verse and al-Sajda 32:51.

QIRAAT-ER:17:83:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:83:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:83:8#1/r1.claim: The metathesized nāʾa form means he rose heavily or pulled away with effort.
QIRAAT-ER:17:83:8#1/r1.anchor: same root n-'-y reversed letter order

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r4.claim: The verse contrasts God's blessing with a person's turning away, arrogance, and ingratitude instead of gratitude.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r4.anchor: أعرض عنه وبعد بجانبه اشمئزازا له وتكبرا عن قرب سماعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r5.claim: Most readers have wa-na'a from na'y, meaning to move away; Ibn Amir reads wa-na'a, treated either as metathesis or as rising up.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ونأى من النأي وهو البعد، وقرأ ابن عامر وناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r6.claim: A line of poetry uses na'a for rising while leaning on the left side.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r6.anchor: وناء في شق الشمال كاهله أي نهض متوكئا على شماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r7.claim: Ya'us means despairing that God will grant favor; here humanity is the generic unbeliever, as in other descriptions of human nature.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r7.anchor: ومعنى يؤسا قنوطا من أن ينعم الله عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p104/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains shakilatihi as a person's direction or side.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p93/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p93/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p93/r4.claim: The verse actively attributes blessing to God but says only that harm touches the person; the Quran likewise does not say “We adorned their evil deeds.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p93/r4.anchor: عندما ذكر النعمة قال: (أنعمنا) بإسناد النعمة إلى نفسه تعالى. وعندما ذكر الشر قال: "وإذا مسه الشر"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p809/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p809/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p809/r2.claim: “What We provided” identifies God as the provider, not people themselves; God attributes blessing and good to Himself, not harm, as the verse illustrates.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p809/r2.anchor: كلمة (رزقناكم) تعني: أن الله تعالى هو الرزاق. فأنفقوا مما رزقكم الله وليس الرزق من أنفسكم

BURHAN:v2p362/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p362/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p362/r5.claim: Despair follows when harm is certainly experienced, while the other passage depicts a person of little patience who turns eagerly to prayer when harm occurs.
BURHAN:v2p362/r5.anchor: فان الياس انما حصل عند تحقق مس الضر له فكان الاتيان باذا ادل على المقصود

ITQAN:v3p245/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p245/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p245/r7.claim: Jinas al-itlaq joins words only by resemblance, with examples including janna/jannatayn, ʿamali/ al-qalin, yuwari, irtad, and the repeated ard and duʿaʾ forms.
ITQAN:v3p245/r7.anchor: ومنها تجنيس الإطلاق بأن يجتمعا في المشابهة فقط كقوله ﴿ وجنى الجنتين ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r7.claim: Al-insān in the verses about turning away after receiving mercy refers to ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r7.anchor: الثامن عشر : الإنسان عتبة بن ربيعة . قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r13.claim: Jānib can mean the heart; turning away with one’s side means turning away in one’s heart from faith.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r13.anchor: الثالث الجنب القلب قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r4.claim: Against lexicographers and exegetes who treat naʾy and buʿd as synonyms, Qur'anic usage distinguishes them: naʾy means turning away, refusing, and shunning, as contexts make explicit.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r4.anchor: النأى يأتي بمعنى الإعراض والصد والإشاحة، بصريح السياق في آياته
